# downpipes-io/engine

> The in-account Cloudflare Worker that backs up Workers KV, R2, Secrets Store, D1 and
> Cloudflare configuration, plus Workers script code and settings, Stream and Images
> inventories and the Artifact Registry inventory, to the frozen downpipe/0.1.0 archive format,
> on a schedule, into the customer's own destination bucket. It is the WRITER half of the
> platform. The offline downpipe Go CLI (a separate repository) is the independent READER and
> the recover-forever moat.

No custody: the engine runs entirely in the customer's own Cloudflare account, never sends
data or a Cloudflare token to the vendor, and holds only public recipient keys plus the signer.
The run master is wrapped to a mandatory offline break-glass key the engine can never unwrap,
so a compromise of the live account cannot read past archives.

Licence: Elastic License v2 (source-available). The downpipe reader is MIT so recovery is
never gated on the vendor. The wire-format identifier downpipe/0.1.0 is frozen and never renamed.

## Architecture

- Entry: src/index.ts (Worker fetch + scheduled handlers). GET /ready is an unauthenticated
  readiness probe; the /admin/* surface is authenticated and reached over a service binding
  from the console.
- Durable Objects: SchedulerDO (schedules, run lock, runlog index) and RunSealDO (per-downpipe
  sliced seal continuation for large environments).
- Crypto and format: src/crypto/* (hybrid X25519 plus ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87 signing, AES-256-GCM)
  and src/format/* (the downpipe/0.1.0 container, canonical JSON, ULID, Merkle frontier, reader).

## Recovery path

Recovery never needs the vendor or Cloudflare. The offline downpipe CLI verifies the signed
chain and freshness, then restores every record, given the archive plus the break-glass identity
and the pinned signer public key. See SPEC.md and RECOVER.md in the downpipe repository.

## Tests

- npm run validate: the bespoke cross-implementation validators (the engine writer reproduced
  against the Go reference vectors, byte for byte). This is the authoritative suite.
- npm run test:runtime: the SchedulerDO concurrency invariants in a real workerd isolate (Miniflare).
- npm run test:vitest: a starter vitest-pool-workers suite exercising the Worker fetch entrypoint
  in real workerd.
- npm run test:property: fast-check property tests over the crypto byte helpers and canonical JSON.
- make demo (or DOWNPIPE_REPO=../downpipe npm run demo): the end-to-end writer to reader demo.

## Pointers

- README.md: capabilities, coverage scope, and the no-custody posture.
- SECURITY.md: disclosure policy and the operational-key risk model.
- docs/DEMO.md: the writer to reader demo, with prerequisites and numbered steps.
- docs/OPERATIONS.md: deployment, large environments, and the licence/update activation ceremony.
